Time: 3 min. Teaching intent: Set the evidence contract.

Time: 3 min. Teaching intent: Retrieve prior knowledge before revealing the method.
Talk track: Can a paper's geometry silently fill a course-case blank?
Expected answer / misconception: No. It is a different specimen unless the equivalence is documented.
Visual: The three conditions identify what must be compared.
[Sources]
R6: NIST, Credibility Consideration for Digital Twins | https://www.nist.gov/publications/credibility-consideration-digital-twins-manufacturing
R8: IEEE TCPMT, Simulation and Experimental Study of Fan-Out Warpage | https://ieeexplore.ieee.org/document/8590768

Time: 4 min. Teaching intent: Teach the mechanism or design rule.
Talk track: A model needs an explicit architecture, dimensions, interconnect scheme, and process stage; a generic label is insufficient. Trace the visual in order: architecture; dimensions; stage. Connect this mechanism to the worked example: For a public fan-out warpage paper, record its specimen and stage separately from the course case. Mark dimensions absent from the class export as not supplied.
Expected answer / misconception: Ask students to explain the link between adjacent elements; a conceptual diagram is not a measurement.
Visual: Native diagram encodes the causal or design relationship.
[Sources]
R6: NIST, Credibility Consideration for Digital Twins | https://www.nist.gov/publications/credibility-consideration-digital-twins-manufacturing
R8: IEEE TCPMT, Simulation and Experimental Study of Fan-Out Warpage | https://ieeexplore.ieee.org/document/8590768

Time: 4 min. Teaching intent: Work the example step by step.
Talk track: Set up the case: For a public fan-out warpage paper, record its specimen and stage separately from the course case. Mark dimensions absent from the class export as not supplied. Identify the starting information, state the reasoning step aloud, then ask what observation would check the conclusion. Stop before the next slide's question is answered.
Expected answer / misconception: Students must identify the input, the inference, and the check. 
Visual: Three-part reasoning path separates the example from its verification.

R6: NIST, Credibility Consideration for Digital Twins | https://www.nist.gov/publications/credibility-consideration-digital-twins-manufacturing

Time: 4 min. Teaching intent: Teach the mechanism or design rule.
Talk track: Constraints, thermal loads, symmetry, and reference state can dominate a result even with identical geometry. Trace the visual in order: fixed / free; load; reference state. Connect this mechanism to the worked example: Two synthetic warpage models use the same stack but different support conditions. Their outputs cannot be compared as a material effect. Boundary: The two-model contrast is synthetic teaching data.
Expected answer / misconception: Ask students to explain the link between adjacent elements; a conceptual diagram is not a measurement.
Visual: Native diagram encodes the causal or design relationship.
[Sources]
R6: NIST, Credibility Consideration for Digital Twins | https://www.nist.gov/publications/credibility-consideration-digital-twins-manufacturing
R8: IEEE TCPMT, Simulation and Experimental Study of Fan-Out Warpage | https://ieeexplore.ieee.org/document/8590768

Time: 4 min. Teaching intent: Teach the mechanism or design rule.
